blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Securitize operates ACRED with permissioned token transfers restricted to KYC-onboarded qualified purchasers and retains transfer-agent freeze and burn authority on behalf of Apollo.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: ACRED has one probable canonical native issuance route on Ethereum and five probable Securitize/Wormhole bridge representations on Avalanche, Ink, Polygon, Solana, and Aptos. Wormhole supplies an external validated messaging layer, but the ACRED-specific manager, adapter, peers, validator threshold, rate limits, and conservation invariant remain unidentified. Destination issuer, administration, and upgrade surfaces are retained below as adverse bridge/common-mode controls rather than counted as independent canonical liabilities.

protocols.name: Wormhole / Securitize interoperability
protocols.note: Wormhole identifies ACRED as a multichain tokenized fund and describes Securitize using its own smart contracts for near-instant native transfers.

controls.label: ACRED Avalanche destination master and upgrade owner

routeChecks.caps: The Avalanche destination cap() returned zero, which the verified implementation treats as uncapped; no aggregate bridge conservation bound was verified.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The shared EOA was owner or MASTER for the Avalanche token and trust service and could immediately replace both implementations. The ACRED-specific Wormhole manager, adapter, peer, and route upgrade owner were not identified.

controls.capDescription: The Avalanche local issuance surface is uncapped at the observed token contract; public ACRED/Wormhole material does not prove that it is restricted to validated transfer receipts.
controls.evidence: At the fixed exact cutoff, this zero-code EOA was owner or MASTER for the Avalanche ACRED token and trust-service deployments. It could call issueTokens, grant or revoke ISSUER, set the one-time token cap, and immediately replace both implementations. cap() returned zero on the destination deployment, which the verified implementation treats as uncapped. The public ACRED/Wormhole material does not prove that these local issuance calls are restricted to Wormhole-validated receipts, so this remains adverse bridge-representation/common-mode exposure rather than a second canonical Mint Authority route.

controls.label: ACRED Solana issuer signer for bridge representation

routeChecks.caps: No finite Token-2022 token cap applies to this issuer path; the exact ACRED Wormhole receipt validation and route-level conservation bound were not identified. Re-adjudicated 2026-09-01 under the ODR-D2 rule at Solana slot 443414051 (api.mainnet-beta.solana.com). Token-2022 mint FubtUcvhSCr3VPXEcxouoQjKQ7NWTCzXyECe76B7L3f8 carries exactly five extensions - metadataPointer, mintCloseAuthority, transferHook, permanentDelegate and tokenMetadata - none of which is a supply ceiling, and Token-2022 has no cap extension at all. mintAuthority and freezeAuthority are both Fr3R4632hv5LU2YNXYMnErnLE1XYMe1KPjR8q91KTYbH and supply is 16526675787 base units at six decimals. No numeric mint ceiling exists on this path, so the fail-closed value is raiseable rather than bounded.

controls.evidence: At Solana slot 432714278, this on-curve signer was a decoded member of ACRED ISSUER role account 8TpJ...2JTV. Transaction 58nd...Szbs at pre-cutoff slot 419520045 proves it invoking the Securitize issuer program, which CPI-minted Token-2022 ACRED through controller PDA Fr3R...TYbH. No finite token cap applies. This issuer surface is retained as adverse bridge-representation exposure because the public sources do not prove that its mint path is restricted to validated Wormhole transfers.

controls.label: ACRED Solana Securitize on-ramp issuer PDA

routeChecks.caps: Re-adjudicated 2026-09-01 under the ODR-D2 rule at Solana slot 443414051 (api.mainnet-beta.solana.com). Token-2022 mint FubtUcvhSCr3VPXEcxouoQjKQ7NWTCzXyECe76B7L3f8 carries exactly five extensions - metadataPointer, mintCloseAuthority, transferHook, permanentDelegate and tokenMetadata - none of which is a supply ceiling, and Token-2022 has no cap extension at all. mintAuthority and freezeAuthority are both Fr3R4632hv5LU2YNXYMnErnLE1XYMe1KPjR8q91KTYbH and supply is 16526675787 base units at six decimals. No numeric mint ceiling exists on this path, so the fail-closed value is raiseable rather than bounded. The on-ramp program's IssueTokens CPI is gated by subscription, NAV, asset-provider and compliance checks, none of which is a contract-enforced supply ceiling this control cannot lift.

controls.evidence: The ACRED ISSUER role also contained this off-curve PDA. It derives exactly from Securitize on-ramp program GQDbg...uS4w with seeds ["on_ramp_authority", WCAg...UEBn] and bump 255. The deployed program's SubscribeDsToken path builds an IssueTokens CPI, subject to its configured subscription, NAV, asset-provider, and compliance checks. The exact Wormhole receipt and conservation path is not identified, so this local issuer remains scoreable under Bridge Risk.

controls.label: ACRED Solana on-ramp admin

routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The system-owned EOA is the on-ramp state admin and can pause the path or change operators, the NAV provider, and the asset-provider configuration governing use of the authorized issuer PDA.

controls.evidence: Before the cutoff, ChangeAdmin set this system-owned EOA as the on-ramp state admin, and the state had no later writes. The deployed program lets the admin pause the path and change operators, the NAV provider, and the asset-provider configuration that governs use of the authorized issuer PDA.

controls.label: ACRED Solana shared program upgrade authority
controls.evidence: At Solana slot 432714278, the issuer, PDA controller, transfer-hook, and ACRED on-ramp programs were all BPF-upgradeable and shared this system-owned single-account upgrade authority. Their ProgramData accounts had no post-cutoff writes, and the authority could replace all four programs immediately with no on-chain delay. This upgrade domain is retained for the Solana bridge representation, not canonical Mint Authority.

controls.label: ACRED Aptos issuer 1

routeChecks.caps: Re-adjudicated 2026-09-01 under the ODR-D2 rule at Aptos ledger version 7029391729 (api.mainnet.aptoslabs.com). On metadata object 0xe528f4df568eb9fff6398adc514bc9585fab397f478972bcbebf1e75dee40a88, ds_token::CustomMetadata.cap is still 0, which the deployed ds_token logic treats as unset/uncapped - the same reading the verified Ethereum DSToken source pins, where setCap requires cap == 0 and _cap > 0. The framework-level 0x1::fungible_asset::ConcurrentSupply.max_value is 340282366920938463463374607431768211455, the u128 sentinel rather than a ceiling, against a current value of 14147628991. No numeric mint ceiling exists, so the fail-closed value is raiseable rather than bounded.

controls.evidence: At Aptos ledger version 6262999136, this ordinary account was one of two Roles.issuers entries. The deployed trust_service code permits an issuer or master to call issue_tokens. CustomMetadata.cap was zero, which the deployed ds_token logic treats as uncapped. The public sources do not prove that this local issuer is restricted to validated Wormhole transfers, so it remains adverse bridge-representation exposure.

routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: This account was trust_service master and owner of the package object. It could administer roles and publish compatible package upgrades immediately; no multisig resource or on-chain timelock was present.

controls.label: ACRED Ethereum source-side master and upgrade owner

routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: The ACRED-specific Wormhole NTT manager, adapter, and peer set for the Ethereum source leg remain unidentified: no NTT manager was resolvable from the token, from the trust service, or from published Securitize/Wormhole material at the observation block, so no authenticated remote or burn-before-credit invariant is asserted for this leg.
routeChecks.caps: At Ethereum block 25881932 on 2026-09-01, ACRED cap() returned zero. The verified DSToken implementation sets cap through setCap(uint256), which requires cap == 0 and _cap > 0, so a zero cap is the source's unset/uncapped state and TokenLibrary.issueTokens receives it as no ceiling. getCap(), maxSupply(), mintCap(), supplyCap(), totalCap(), mintingLimit(), MAX_SUPPLY(), CAP(), mintLimit(), totalSupplyCap(), bridgeLimit(), rateLimit(), dailyLimit(), limit(), and maxLimit() all reverted. totalSupply() was 0x60bfeeaac and totalIssued() 0x150196f760 over 27 registered wallets. This control can therefore issue without a ceiling today.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The token is an ERC1967 proxy (170 bytes) whose implementation slot held DSToken 0xfc8a9000c161e3c6e073e967107ce926a44a06e2 and whose admin slot was zero, i.e. a UUPS proxy upgraded through owner(). owner() returned 0x59c1eacec450c57dcb9b8725d0f96635c2b676ee, an address with zero code. The token's TRUST_SERVICE (service id 1) resolved to 0xc397436742eaf7c325ddbfc4dc63d95822b27101 — itself an ERC1967 proxy over 0xd5417b82ae5b9ab7db1532b517fb284f38d7141e — and its getRole(0x59c1eacec450c57dcb9b8725d0f96635c2b676ee) returned 1, ROLE_MASTER. isPaused() returned false. One externally owned key therefore holds master role, issuance administration and immediate upgrade authority on the source deployment, with no timelock and no multisig.

controls.capDescription: The Ethereum source deployment is uncapped at the observed block and this key can also set the one-time cap, grant ROLE_ISSUER, and replace the token implementation; public ACRED/Wormhole material does not prove that source-side issuance is restricted to validated transfer receipts.
bypassSurfaces: The same key is ROLE_MASTER on the trust service, so it can grant itself or others any DSToken role, and it holds the UUPS upgrade path on the token proxy.

controls.evidence: The Ethereum deployment is ACRED's canonical native issuance route and also the source leg for the five Securitize/Wormhole representations, but it carried no bridge control until now. At Ethereum block 25881932 on 2026-09-01 the same zero-code key that is destination master on Avalanche, Ink, Polygon, Solana and Aptos — 0x59c1eAcEc450c57Dcb9b8725d0F96635C2b676Ee — is also the source-side owner() of the ACRED proxy and ROLE_MASTER on its trust service 0xc397436742eaf7c325ddbfc4dc63d95822b27101. The proxy's admin slot is zero, so the upgrade path is UUPS through that owner, and cap() is zero, which the verified DSToken treats as uncapped. Because the ACRED-specific Wormhole manager and peer set are still unidentified, the source-side burn or lock that should conserve supply against the destination mints is unproven; this control is retained as adverse common-mode bridge exposure across all six ACRED deployments rather than as a second canonical liability.
